title: Add experiment config propagation lag/staleness metrics
author: Logan Wright
description: Motivation: We’ve had multiple reports (staging + early beta) of Console results appearing stale and/or routing decisions not reflecting recent experiment config edits. Today we can infer this indirectly from logs and a few cache hit-rate metrics, but we don’t have a first-class signal for “how far behind is the data plane from the control plane” and “are we serving configs older than our intended staleness bound”. This PR introduces a small set of canonical propagation-lag and staleness metrics for route experiments, emitted from the router/policy-evaluator, and wires them into the standard OTel metrics pipeline so they can be used for dashboards + alerting. What’s included: (1) New metrics emitted on config fetch/apply path: redwood.experiments.config_propagation_lag_seconds (histogram), redwood.experiments.config_version_age_seconds (histogram), redwood.experiments.config_stale_reads_total (counter), redwood.experiments.config_last_good_version_timestamp_seconds (gauge), redwood.experiments.config_apply_errors_total (counter). (2) Metric semantics: propagation_lag = now() - config.published_at (as stamped by control plane) at the moment we apply a config snapshot; version_age = now() - config.version_created_at (helps detect long-lived “stuck” versions even if republished); stale_read is incremented when version_age exceeds the router’s configured max_staleness_seconds OR when we fall back to last-known-good due to fetch failure. (3) Dimensions are intentionally limited to avoid cardinality blowups: {region, environment, route_id_normalized} only. We do NOT tag by experiment_id/variant_id. (4) Dashboard exposure: metrics are exported via existing otel-metrics pipeline under the experiments namespace; Grafana dashboards/alerts are tracked in observability-pack (separate PR), but this PR includes the naming + units that those dashboards assume. (5) Draft alert thresholds (not enabled here, for SRE review): Warning if p95(config_propagation_lag_seconds) > 60s for 10m in any region; Critical if p95 > 300s for 5m OR stale_reads_total rate > 1% of config_reads for 10m. These thresholds are intended to align with the control-plane propagation SLO work-in-progress and to be tuned post-beta. Testing: unit tests for lag computation (published_at missing, clock skew guard), integration test that simulates config update and validates histogram observation, and a benchmark check to ensure no significant overhead in the hot path. Notes: This PR is additive and safe to roll out behind existing experiment feature flags; metrics emission occurs regardless of whether a request is assigned to a variant (it’s tied to config apply, not request processing). Related: Slack thread 1736039442-route-experiments-config-propagation-lag, ENG-9023 caching/propagation controls, and SUP-24910 (Console results not updating).
commits: otel/experiments: add metric instruments and naming conventions
router/experiments: compute propagation lag and version age on config apply
router/experiments: emit stale-read counters on last-known-good fallback path
tests: add unit tests for timestamps + missing fields; add integration test for lag observation
docs(internal): add metric definitions to experiments telemetry README
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Can we confirm units and bucket boundaries for the histograms? We’ve had issues where defaults made p95 meaningless. Also please document the exact dimension set; dashboards will assume it.

Logan Wright (author): Good call. Added explicit view config for config_propagation_lag_seconds and config_version_age_seconds (buckets: 1s, 5s, 10s, 30s, 60s, 120s, 300s, 600s). Also updated internal docs with dimensions and an explicit “no experiment_id/variant_id tagging” note.

Sean Gallagher: Two concerns: (1) how do we handle control-plane clock skew vs data-plane? (2) we need a metric for ‘last known good’ usage because that’s operationally distinct from being merely behind.

Logan Wright (author): Added a clamp to 0 when now < published_at (treat as 0 lag and emit config_apply_errors_total with reason=clock_skew_suspected). Also added config_stale_reads_total with reason=last_known_good_fallback and a gauge for last_good_version_timestamp_seconds so we can see when we’re pinned to a snapshot.
Jordan Lee: route_id_normalized dimension: are we using the same normalization as attribution (template path) or raw route key? Raw paths will be a cardinality bomb.
Logan Wright (author): Using normalized route ID from the routing policy layer (template-style ID). Added a small comment + test that ensures we never attach raw path.
Rafael Mendes: Draft thresholds look aggressive for beta. Can we separate ‘propagation lag’ from ‘aggregation lag’ so on-call isn’t chasing the wrong thing?

Logan Wright (author): Agreed; this PR is only data-plane config propagation. Updated docs to call out non-goals (analytics rollups). The alert threshold text is now labeled “draft” and includes guidance to correlate with aggregation job delay metrics before declaring Console stale results as propagation-related.
Allison Grant: Please add to the metrics allowlist and confirm we won’t exceed our standard tag policy.
Logan Wright (author): Added to allowlist_experiments.yaml and kept tags at {region, environment, route_id_normalized}.
Sean Gallagher: Approving with note that enabling alerts should be a separate PR after SLO doc lands.
Rafael Mendes: Approved; please link runbook once created (ENG-9033).
release_notes: Added first-class metrics for route experiment config propagation lag and stale-config fallback usage to support dashboards and alerting.
